note: A content pack, not a hand-written page. Updating the program listing is editing this file — the same shape a teacher would use to update a games pack. Nothing below has run yet; this is the proposed calendar, in TechCentral's own session formats (My Digital Life = 60-minute standalone for adults, Maker Monday = 90 minutes, Makerlab = 60-90 for kids/teens, Tech Help 1-on-1 = 2-hour blocks). This sample site does not replace the library's own calendar — every entry links to the real public LibCal calendar, since none of these sessions has a scheduled date or its own event page yet.

sessions.title: Upcycle Your Old Device
sessions.summary: Turn a phone or tablet headed for a drawer into a small library dashboard — a clock, a rotating quote and fact, one tap into a learning game.

sessions.title: AAC Boards 101: Set Up and Use a Communication Board
sessions.cadence: Monthly, standalone — no signup series required
sessions.summary: Build a real communication board from scratch, in the browser, on a library computer. Leave with something you or a family member could use the same day.

sessions.title: Makerlab: Design Your Own AAC Board (Kids & Teens)
sessions.summary: The same board editor, aimed younger: pick symbols, arrange a board around a hobby or a favorite game, and try it with a switch or a game controller instead of a mouse.

sessions.title: Connect a Switch: Device Setup & Calibration
sessions.summary: What a switch actually is, how it plugs into a browser with no special drivers, and how to tune hold time and repeat so it fits a specific hand, cheek, or head movement.

sessions.title: Maker Monday: 3D-Print an Adaptive Switch Enclosure
sessions.cadence: Quarterly — needs the makerspace's printers booked
sessions.summary: Design and print an enclosure for an arcade button and a microcontroller — a roughly $15 DIY adaptive switch, using the makerspace's own printers. The design is not built yet; this session is where it gets designed.

sessions.title: Tech Help 1-on-1: Personalize a Communication Board
sessions.summary: One patron, one board, one hour and a half to two hours: real vocabulary for their own life, their own switch or pointing method, and enough troubleshooting to leave confident.

sessions.title: Games for the Classroom: Trivia, Word Forge & Algebra
sessions.summary: Three accessible learning games a teacher or homeschool parent can reconfigure on the spot — different word lists, different difficulty, different subject — without touching any code.

sessions.title: Build Your Own Local AI: What's Coming
sessions.cadence: One-time preview, once the module ships
sessions.summary: A syllabus-only preview of a course that doesn't exist yet: running a small AI model on your own machine so nothing about how you communicate ever has to leave it.

sessions.title: Learn to Play Scan-and-Select Bingo
sessions.summary: A bingo game played entirely by switch-scanning — highlight, wait, select — the same input pattern behind the communication boards, taught through play. Not built yet; listed here as what's next.
